dedupe_keys.name: iot enabled waste collection pilot in lahore pakistan waste management 2 0

description: This case reports a pilot of sensor-based waste collection in Lahore, Pakistan, in which bins report their fill level and collection routes are optimised in real time. The system combines an ultrasonic fill-level sensor prototype, city-wide LoRaWAN and cellular connectivity, a cloud platform for storing and analysing readings, and routing algorithms that plan collection to reduce time, distance and fuel. The producers are Addas, Khan and Naseer, publishing in PLOS ONE (2024). Coverage is ten pilot locations across Lahore. The authors report that the pilots handled more than 200 million data points and, against conventional practice, improved route efficiency by 32 percent, reduced fuel use and emissions by 29 percent, increased waste processing throughput by 33 percent and cut vehicle maintenance costs by 18 percent. The article is open access under CC BY. Caveats: the gains are the authors' own figures, the sensor data and routing code are not released with the article, the baseline for comparison is not detailed in the abstract, and the pilot period is not stated there. Simulation uses: parameters for sensor-driven collection in waste logistics and city digital twin models, and scenarios where connectivity or fuel supply is disrupted. Related records: the NYC waste characterisation study (data-dsny-waste-characterization) gives waste composition for a city system.
